what_it_is.prose: Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) is the wholly-owned defence subsidiary of Tata Sons Private Limited, founded in 2007. TASL is unlisted and does not publicly disclose revenue or order book. The company operates across four major business lines: (1) Aerostructures and MRO — TASL is the partner for Airbus C-295 final assembly line in Vadodara (₹21,935 crore programme, 40 of 56 aircraft to be built by TASL in India), Lockheed Martin C-130J MRO facility (groundbreaking December 2025, operations early 2027), and Boeing AH-64 Apache fuselage assembly via Tata Boeing International Limited (TBIL); (2) Land systems — TASL is the co-developer with DRDO of the WhAP 8x8 Wheeled Armoured Platform (Tata Kestrel), which became the first Indian-designed armoured vehicle to be exported when the first batch was delivered to the Royal Moroccan Army on 24 December 2025; (3) Missile systems integration — TASL manufactures the Akash Army Launcher (AAL), Akash Air Force Launcher (AAFL), Advanced Air Defence (AAD) Mobile Launcher System for ballistic missile defence, and MRSAM Army launchers, all in partnership with DRDO; and (4) Artillery — TASL is the manufacturing partner for the ATAGS Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System (123 guns of the 307-gun March 2025 ₹6,900 crore MoD contract, ~₹2,760 crore Tata share). TASL also produces UAVs (Sky-I, Rakshak VTOL, Advanced Loitering Systems).

deployments_procurement.summary: TASL's major programme commitments include the WhAP 8x8 (Indian Army limited + Royal Moroccan Army export, first batch delivered 24 December 2025), ATAGS (123 guns of 307 total, March 2025 ₹6,900 crore MoD contract — ~₹2,760 crore Tata share), Airbus C-295 (40 aircraft to be built by TASL in India, ₹21,935 crore total programme), Akash launchers (AAL and AAFL, joint with DRDO), AAD MLS for ballistic missile defence, MRSAM Army launchers, and the C-130J MRO facility (groundbreaking December 2025).

faq.question: What was significant about the WhAP 8x8 export to Morocco?
faq.answer: The first batch of WhAP 8x8 (Wheeled Armoured Platform, also called Tata Kestrel) armoured vehicles was delivered to the Royal Moroccan Army on 24 December 2025 — the first export of an Indian-designed armoured vehicle. The WhAP 8x8 was co-developed by TASL with DRDO. The export demonstrates Indian private-sector land systems capability and opens the door for further Indian armoured vehicle exports to friendly foreign countries.

faq.question: What is TASL's role in the C-295 programme?
faq.answer: Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) is the Indian final assembly partner for the Airbus C-295 transport aircraft programme, signed on 24 September 2021 for ₹21,935 crore (~$2.5 billion). Of the 56 aircraft, 16 are imported fly-away from Airbus Seville (Spain) and 40 are assembled by TASL at a dedicated Final Assembly Line (FAL) in Vadodara, Gujarat — the first private commercial transport aircraft FAL in India. The first India-built C-295 was rolled out in October 2025.

faq.question: Why is TASL's revenue and order book not publicly disclosed?
faq.answer: TASL is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Tata Sons Private Limited, which is itself unlisted. As a result, TASL is not required to publicly disclose revenue, profit, or order book. Material contract values are visible in MoD press releases — for example, the ATAGS share (123 guns of 307 total, ₹2,760 crore Tata share of the March 2025 ₹6,900 crore MoD deal) and the C-295 programme (₹21,935 crore total). Atlas should mark financial details as 'n/a — unlisted subsidiary of unlisted Tata Sons'.
